Rashi on Chullin 2b:1:1.hebrew: אבל אמר הרי עלי לא - דלמא פשע ולא מקיים, והכי מוקמינן לה בנדרים בפ"ק (דף י.), לר' יהודה תני נודב ומשלם. אלמא מעריכין ונודרין לכתחלה לא, דהרי עלי הוא דליכא למימר בהו הרי זו, עד דאמר ברישא ערכי עלי והדר יהיב כפי הקצוב בפרשה. ודמי עלי נמי דבעי למשיימיה כעבדא, דהיכי מצי למימר הרי אלו לערכים אם לא נדר תחלה בערך:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:1:1.english: But if he said, "It is incumbent upon me" [harei alai] - no - Because perhaps he will be negligent and not fulfill it. And this is how we establish it in [tractate] Nedarim, in the first chapter (10a): according to Rabbi Yehuda, [the mishna] teaches, "one who pledges [a gift offering] and pays it." This shows that with regard to valuation-vows and worth-vows, [designating a specific item] is not [done] ab initio, because it is specifically with "harei alai" that one cannot say "harei zo" ["this one"] about these - rather, he must first say, "My valuation is incumbent upon me," and only afterward give the amount fixed in the Torah portion. And likewise with "my worth is incumbent upon me," which requires appraising him like a slave - for how could he say, "These are designated for valuations," if he had not first vowed by way of a valuation?

Rashi on Chullin 2b:2:1.english: And is every instance of "all" not [said] with reference to an act performed ab initio? - That is: is there no case where [the word] "all" is said with reference to an act performed ab initio?

Rashi on Chullin 2b:2:2.english: All are obligated in the sukkah - This comes to include a minor who no longer needs his mother['s constant care].

Rashi on Chullin 2b:2:3.english: All are obligated in tzitzit - This comes to include a minor who knows how to wrap himself [in a garment].

Rashi on Chullin 2b:3:1.hebrew: חייבין לא קאמינא - היכא דתני חייבין, מוכח ודאי דלכתחלה קאמר:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:3:1.english: I am not speaking [of cases] where it says "obligated" - Wherever [a Mishnah or baraita] teaches the term "chayavin" (obligated), it certainly proves that it is speaking of doing so ab initio (lechatchila).

Rashi on Chullin 2b:3:2.hebrew: הכל סומכין - לאתויי יורש, והא ודאי לכתחלה קאמר, דמצוה רמיא עליה על כרחיה:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:3:2.english: All place hands [on the offering] - This comes to include an heir [who inherited an animal his father had consecrated]. And this [word "all"] certainly indicates that it is permitted ab initio, since the mitzva is imposed upon him whether he wants it or not.

Rashi on Chullin 2b:5:1.hebrew: תרתי דיעבד למה לי - הכי איבעי ליה למיתני שחיטת הכל כשרה חוץ מחש"ו, דמשמע שפיר דהנך דמרבינן מהכל דיעבד קמרבינן אבל לא לכתחלה. א"נ ניתני הכל שוחטין לחודיה, כדתנן גבי מעריכין ונודרין, ולא מפרש, למה לי למיתני הכל שוחטין ואצטריך לפרושי ושחיטתן כשרה למימר דשוחטין דרישא דיעבד הוא. ואי קשיא בתמורה נמי הא תני והדר מפרש - התם לא קתני כה"ג הכל ממירין ותמורתן תמורה בהדי הדדי. ואי משום לא שאדם רשאי, משום דבעי לאסוקי וסופג את הארבעים לאשמועינן דלוקין על לאו שאין בו מעשה:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:5:1.english: Why do I need two [expressions of] after-the-fact [validity]? - It should rather have taught: "The slaughtering of all is valid, except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor," which would properly imply that these [extended categories] which we include under "all" are included only after the fact, but not ab initio. Alternatively, let it teach "all may slaughter" alone, as we learned regarding those who make personal valuations and those who make vows, without any further explanation - why need it teach "all may slaughter" and then need to explain further with "and their slaughtering is valid," to say that the "may slaughter" of the first clause means after the fact? And if you raise a difficulty [from the fact] that by substitution (temurah) too, [the Mishnah] teaches [something] and then explains - there, it does not teach in this manner "all may substitute, and their substitution is a valid substitution" together [as two parallel clauses]. And if [you object] because of [the phrase] "not that a person is permitted [to substitute]" - that is because it needs to go on to [teach] "and he receives forty lashes," to teach us that one is lashed for [violating] a prohibition that involves no action.

Tosafot on Chullin 2b:1:1.hebrew: אבל אמר הרי עלי לא - הך סוגיא כלישנא בתרא דפ"ק דנדרים (דף י.), דקאמר דפליגי בנודב, אבל ללישנא קמא דקאמר דפליגי בנודר, אבל בנודב מודה רבי מאיר. וא"ת: כיון דקרא בנדר כתיב, מנא ליה לרבי מאיר דאין נודב טוב מנודר ומשלם? ולרבי יהודה נמי אמאי, אם אמר הרי עלי לא, הא כל היכא דכתיב נדר הוי נדר דוקא, ונדבה הוי נדבה דוקא, כדמוכח בריש מנחות (דף ב.) וזבחים (דף ב.) גבי "כאשר נדרת לה' אלהיך" נדבה, דפריך: האי נדבה נדר הוא! וי"מ דהתם פריך משום דשני קרא בדבוריה. וי"ל דקסבר, כיון דחייש קרא לתקלה בנדר, ה"ה בנדבה, דהא איכא למיחש לתקלה, דאפי' מביאה לעזרה ומקדישה יכול להנות ולמעול בה, ולבא לידי תקלה בכמה עניינים, דכ"ע לא בקיאי כהלל, דמעולם לא מעל אדם בעולתו (פסחים דף סו:). ולרבי יהודה נמי משמע ליה קרא דוקא בנדבה, אע"ג דבנדר כתיב, דהא בנדר לא מצי למימר דנודר ומשלם טוב, שהרי כתיב "וכי תחדל לנדור לא יהיה בך חטא", הא אם תדור יהיה בך חטא. וללישנא קמא דנדרים מפרשינן לקרא: הא אם תדור אפשר שיהיה בך חטא אם לא תשלם. וא"ת: לרבי מאיר דאין טוב שיהא נודב ומשלם כל עיקר, אפילו מביא כבשתו לעזרה, להאי לישנא בתרא דנדרים, היאך אכלו ישראל שלמים במדבר? וי"ל, כיון שנאסרו בענין אחר בבשר, הוו כאילו צוה להם המקום לאכול על ידי שלמים. וא"ת: והא כתיב (בראשית כ״ח:כ׳) "וידר יעקב נדר", וכתיב (יונה ב׳:י׳) "את אשר נדרתי אשלמה"? וי"ל דבשעת צרה שרי, כדאמרינן בבראשית רבה: "וידר יעקב נדר" - "לאמר" "לאמר" לדורות, שיהיו נודרים בעת צרה:
Tosafot on Chullin 2b:1:1.english: But if he said, "It is incumbent upon me," no - This sugya follows the later version [lishna basra] found at the beginning of Nedarim (10a), which states that Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda disagree with regard to one who makes a donation (nodev). But according to the first version [lishna kama], which states that they disagree with regard to one who makes a vow (noder), but with regard to one who donates, Rabbi Meir concedes [that he may pay with money instead]. And if you should ask: since the verse is written with regard to a vow, from where does Rabbi Meir derive that it is not "good" for one who donates to pay [with money] instead? And according to Rabbi Yehuda too, why, if he said "It is incumbent upon me," is the answer no - is it not so that wherever "neder" (vow) is written it means specifically a vow, and "nedavah" (donation) means specifically a donation, as is proven at the beginning of Menachot (2a) and Zevachim (2a), regarding [the verse] "as you have vowed to the Lord your God," [said in the context of] a donation, where it asks: is this "donation" [really] a "vow"? And some explain that there it asks [that question] because the verse switches its wording midway. And [we] can answer that he [Rabbi Meir] holds that since the verse is concerned about mishap in the case of a vow, the same applies to a donation - for there, too, one may be concerned about mishap: even if one brings the animal to the Temple courtyard and consecrates it, he may still derive benefit from it and commit trespass (me'ilah) with it, and come to mishap in various ways, since not everyone is as expert [in the laws of me'ilah] as Hillel, of whom it is said that no man ever committed trespass with his own burnt-offering (Pesachim 66b). And according to Rabbi Yehuda too, the verse implies [that it is referring] specifically to a donation, even though it is written regarding a vow - for in the case of a vow he could not say that one who vows and then pays [with money] is "good," since it is written, "but if you refrain from vowing, there will be no sin in you," implying that if you do vow, there will be sin in you. And according to the first version [lishna kama] of Nedarim, we explain the verse [to mean]: if you vow, it is possible that there will be sin in you - if you do not pay [what you vowed]. And if you should ask: according to Rabbi Meir, that it is not good at all for one to donate and then pay [with money] instead - even if he brings his ewe-lamb to the Temple courtyard - according to this later version of Nedarim, how did the Israelites eat peace-offerings (shelamim) in the wilderness [since all such offerings would then involve donating and paying, which should be improper]? And [we] can answer: since they were forbidden to eat meat in any other way, it is as though the Omnipresent had commanded them to eat by means of peace-offerings. And if you should ask: but is it not written (Genesis 28:20), "And Jacob vowed a vow," and it is written (Jonah 2:10), "That which I have vowed I will pay"? And [we] can answer that in a time of distress it is permitted, as we say in Bereishit Rabbah: [regarding the verse] "And Jacob vowed a vow, saying (leimor)" - the word "leimor" [is written twice, once here and once elsewhere,] teaching [that this applies] for [all] generations, that one may make vows in a time of distress.

Rashi on Chullin 2b:6:1.hebrew: הכי קתני - לכתחלה ודיעבד, דמתניתין הכל שוחטין לכתחלה, לאתויי טמא בחולין:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:6:1.english: This is what it is teaching - [It is speaking of a distinction between] ab initio and after the fact, for our Mishnah's [statement] "all may slaughter" [refers to] ab initio, [and it comes] to include a tamei person [slaughtering] non-sacred [animals].

Rashi on Chullin 2b:6:2.english: It is obvious - For Israel was never commanded regarding the purity of their non-sacred [food].

Rashi on Chullin 2b:6:3.hebrew: שנעשו על טהרת קדש - דקבל עליה לאכול בטהרת קדש, שרוצה להרגיל עצמו בטהרת קדשים, שאם יאכל שלמים או תודה יהא בקי בשמירתן:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:6:3.english: That were made in the purity of sacred [food] - [This means] that he has taken upon himself to eat [non-sacred food] in the state of purity required for sacred [food], because he wants to accustom himself to the purity of sacred items, so that if he [later] eats peace-offerings or a thanks-offering, he will be expert in observing their [purity requirements].

Rashi on Chullin 2b:6:4.hebrew: כקדש דמו - וחייב להבדל מדרבנן מכל טומאות הפוסלות בהן, ואפילו הכי (שחיט טמא) לכתחלה, ובסכין ארוכה, כדמפרש:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:6:4.english: Its blood is like consecrated [food] - He [who prepares his non-sacred food according to the purity of consecrated food] is obligated, by rabbinic law, to keep away from all the impurities that disqualify consecrated food. And even so, a tamei person may slaughter it ab initio, and with a long knife, as [the Gemara] will explain.

Rashi on Chullin 2b:8:1.hebrew: ובמוקדשין - לכתחלה לא ישחוט, ואפילו בסכין ארוכה, כיון דמוזהר מן התורה שלא יטמא, כדכתיב (במדבר יח) ואני הנה נתתי לך את משמרת תרומותי, אלמא בעינן שמירה, גזור בהו רבנן לכתחלה, משום לך לך אמרינן נזירא, סחור סחור לכרמא לא תקרב:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:8:1.english: And with regard to sacrificial [animals] - Ab initio he should not slaughter, even with a long knife, since he is warned by the Torah not to become impure, as it is written (Numbers 18), "And I, behold, I have given you the charge of My gifts," which indicates that we require [him to exercise] care [to avoid impurity]. [Therefore] the Rabbis decreed concerning them, ab initio, [that he not slaughter even with a long knife], because of [the principle that] we say to a nazirite: "Go around, go around, but do not approach the vineyard."

Tosafot on Chullin 2b:5:1.hebrew: אנא "שחיטתן כשרה" קא קשיא לי - משמע שרב אשי הקשה אותה קושיא, ואע"פ שהיא סוגיית הגמרא. ומכאן ראיה שרב אשי סידר הגמרא, אע"ג דאביי ורבא נמי אתו לשנויי הך קושיא, והם קדמו הרבה לרב אשי - שמא גם בימיהם הקשוה כבר:
Tosafot on Chullin 2b:5:1.english: I was troubled by [the words] "their slaughter is valid" - This implies that Rav Ashi himself raised this question, even though it is [presented as] a sugya of the Gemara [i.e., stated anonymously]. And from here there is proof that Rav Ashi arranged the Gemara - even though Abaye and Rava also came to answer this very question, and they preceded Rav Ashi by a great deal; perhaps in their days, too, this question had already been raised.

Tosafot on Chullin 2b:6:1.hebrew: טמא בחולין מאי למימרא - ואע"ג דאסור לגרום טומאה לחולין שבא"י, היינו דוקא בפירות דשייכא בהו תרומה, אבל בשר לא. ואפילו יהא אסור לטמאות גופו באוכלין טמאין, כדדרשינן: "והתקדשתם והייתם קדושים" - אזהרה לבני ישראל שיאכלו חוליהן בטהרה, מכל מקום יכול לטמאותן ולאוכלן בימי טומאתו:
Tosafot on Chullin 2b:6:1.english: A tamei person [slaughtering] non-sacred [animals] - what does this come to teach? - Even though it is forbidden to cause tumah to non-sacred produce in Eretz Yisrael, that is specifically with regard to fruit, to which teruma applies, but not meat. And even though it may be forbidden for a person to render his own body tamei by eating tamei foods, as we expound: "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy" - a warning to the Jewish people that they should eat their non-sacred food in purity - nevertheless, he may render the meat tamei and eat it during the days of his own tumah.

Rashi on Chullin 2b:8:2.english: Their slaughter is valid - This refers to the after-the-fact [ruling] of the Mishnah. And further on, [the Gemara] explains why [it does] not [reason that] the person renders the knife tamei, and then [the knife], in turn, renders the flesh tamei.

Tosafot on Chullin 2b:8:1.hebrew: ובמוקדשין לא ישחוט שמא יגע בבשר - אע"ג דאמרינן לקמן (חולין דף קכא:) דמפרכסת הרי היא כחיה, חיישינן שמא יגע אחר פירכוס. א"נ, דוקא לענין העמדה והערכה הויא כחיה, אבל לענין טומאה, כיון ששחט שנים או רוב שנים מקבלת טומאה, דחשיב אוכל, כדאמר בהעור והרוטב (לקמן שם): השוחט בהמה טמאה לעובד כוכבים ומפרכסת, מטמאה טומאת אוכלין אבל לא טומאת נבילות:
Tosafot on Chullin 2b:8:1.english: And with consecrated animals he should not slaughter, lest he touch the flesh - Even though we say further on (Chullin 121b) that an animal which is convulsing [after slaughter] is considered as [still] alive, [nonetheless] we are concerned lest he touch it after the convulsing [has stopped]. Alternatively, it is specifically with regard to the matter of standing and being appraised [i.e., having its value assessed] that it is considered as [still] alive, but with regard to tumah (ritual impurity), since he has slaughtered two [of the requisite organs] or the majority of two, it becomes susceptible to tumah, for it is considered food - as is stated in [the chapter] HaOr VeHarotev (ibid.): one who slaughters a non-kosher animal for a non-Jew, and it convulses, it becomes tamei with the tumah of foods, but not with the tumah of a carcass.
